transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-13
Start: 09:21 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jared (Redwood SE), Priya (Sparrow HoM), Kenzo (Sparrow Platform), Lidia (Sparrow Product), Samir (SRE, joined 00:12)

Summary: Quick recap of last week's run, focus on tokens per dollar, caching impact, and batching tradeoffs. Action items captured at end.

Topics: tokens/sec per dollar, prefix caching savings, KV cache behavior, batching size/latency tradeoffs, dedicated vs hosted economics, security questions (KMS, SSO).

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): all right everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight, today's goal is to go over the numbers jared ran and decide the next benchmark matrix.
[00:20] Priya (Sparrow): thanks, and quick heads up, we're still seeing that initial spike in the morning window so the tokens per request distribution skews quite a bit so apologies if some of our numbers look noisy.
[00:34] Jared (Redwood SE): yeah no worries, that's why we looked at p50/p95 and also tokens/sec per dollar because p50 alone hides cost. I have the exported run, i'll share the sheet after the call.
[01:02] Kenzo (Sparrow): one quick infrastructure note — our current trial is on-hosted, not VPC. if we move to Dedicated or Private we might change network latencies, just flagging.
[01:18] Maya: good call, we'll include a dedicated baseline in the pricing notes.
[01:30] Lidia: can we get a reminder of what 'prefix caching' means in the run? i saw numbers but want to be sure we're comparing apples to apples.
[01:47] Jared: sure — prefix caching here is partial caching of repeated initial tokens and KV cache reuse across requests; it reduces generation token count for repeated prompts. in the first run we had prefix caching off, KV cache was warm for the single-client flow but not across parallel clients.
[02:12] Priya: ok so when you say KV cache warm/unwarm that's like the past conversation where similar sessions share the same key value memory?
[02:25] Jared: exactly, though the transcription sometimes says 'K V cash' which is funny, but yes it's the kv cache. if requests hit similar prefixes we saw up to ~22% fewer generated tokens. that translated to roughly 18% tokens per dollar improvement in the hosted run.
[02:48] Maya: interesting — was that consistent across different prompt lengths?
[02:56] Jared: it's variable. for short prompts (<150 tokens) savings are smaller, around 8-10%. for long instructions with repeated system context we got closer to 20-25%. also for multi-turn chat style requests prefix caching helps a lot.
[03:20] Priya: that's promising. our workload is mostly short Q&A but there is a large tail of multi-turn support flows, so a mixed result makes sense.
[03:34] Samir (SRE, joined): sorry late — is there a note about batching and latency I should be aware of? our infra team is cautious about adding batching that could bump tail latency.
[03:47] Jared: yeah batching tradeoffs came up. we tested batch sizes 1, 16, 64. tokens/sec scales roughly linearly up to 16, then diminishing returns. 64 gave ~2.8x throughput vs 1 but added 80-120ms median latency and larger tail. depending on your SLOs, smaller batches with aggressive async concurrency may be the sweet spot.
[04:16] Kenzo: so for our customer-facing API we want p95 under 400ms. did any batch configs meet that?
[04:27] Jared: batch 16 with the current runtime and model quantization hit p95 ~320ms on Dedicated hardware. hosted had similar but slightly higher — ~350ms. batch 64 pushed p95 over 500ms so not ideal.
[04:43] Priya: and tokens/sec per dollar — how much better was 16 vs 1?
[04:50] Jared: roughly 1.9x tokens/sec per dollar at batch 16 vs 1, considering both GPU utilization and reduced per-request overhead. batch 64 gave ~2.6x but remember the latency penalty.
[05:08] Lidia: are those numbers normalized to the same model and quantization? i.e., same 8-bit quant profile?
[05:16] Jared: yes, same model checkpoint and q8_0 quant profile for the comparison. we also ran a q4_0 run which lowered cost further but increased variance and slightly higher latency tail.
[05:33] Maya: okay let's talk about the unit economics. your initial ask was tokens/sec per dollar and tokens per user, right, Priya?
[05:42] Priya: yes, we want to project monthly spend for 200k monthly active users with average 120 tokens per session and an expected 15% multi-turn follow-ups.
[05:55] Jared: using the hosted baseline without caching and batch1 that's roughly X tokens / dollar — (note: placeholder) — but with prefix caching and batch 16 we can reduce that by ~48% in the best-case mix, realistically 30-35% given your mix.
[06:18] Priya: wow that's big, can you unpack the 48%? what's the breakdown?
[06:25] Jared: about 22% from prefix/KV caching for repetitive system/prompt content, ~35% from batching and utilization improvements, minus a small delta for extra latency or q-level tradeoffs. so combined it compounds but not perfectly additive, so real-world we estimate 30-35% improvement.
[06:47] Kenzo: does that assume no additional infra costs for cache warming or extra memory on the GPU?
[06:55] Jared: it assumes the standard Redis-like prefix cache and the runtime's in-GPU kv cache; memory overhead is modest but for large context sizes you need slightly bigger instance types. we'll include the resource delta in the next benchmark.
[07:10] Lidia: any concerns about model quality changes when using q4_0 or q8_0 quantization?
[07:18] Jared: for most of your intents we saw negligible qualitative difference at q8_0. q4_0 started to show minor hallucination frequency increase in open-ended tasks; we'll put a few eval prompts in the next run to quantify.
[07:32] Priya: perfect, please include a few of our QA prompts in the eval.
[07:36] Jared: noted.
[07:40] Maya: security question — Priya, you had asked about KMS and logs retention — any updates on requirements?
[07:48] Priya: for compliance we'll need encryption at rest with customer-managed keys or HSM; audit logs for inference requests kept 90 days; and SSO/SAML for team access. SOC2 is a nice-to-have but not a blocker at the moment.
[08:05] Maya: good — we have a private deployment playbook that covers KMS/HSM and audit logs, i'll share that.
[08:12] Kenzo: one minor thing — if we go to Private deployment, does the Redwood control plane still need internet egress? we're an air-gapped possibility.
[08:22] Jared: Private can be configured in a few modes; for air-gapped we have an on-prem package, though that adds lead time and licensing. we'll outline options in the security doc.
[08:37] Lidia: back to economics — can you show an example projection for our 200k MAU? maybe a high/med/low scenario.
[08:46] Jared: yes — i have three projections in the sheet. rough numbers: low usage (50k MAU) hosted baseline $6k/mo; med (200k MAU) hosted baseline $22k/mo; med with caching+batching ~ $14k/mo; Dedicated reserved capacity reduces unit cost further to maybe $10-12k/mo depending on commit. all approximations, we'll run a formal calc once we have your prompt set.
[09:14] Priya: that's helpful. I noticed you said hosted baseline — do you assume a particular model size?
[09:21] Jared: we used the 34B family that you trialed last week, with the q8_0 profile in the baseline. we can model a smaller 7B for cheaper but quality tradeoffs.
[09:34] Kenzo: for the Dedicated numbers, is there a recommended autoscaling config? we don't want to overcommit.
[09:42] Maya: we usually recommend a mix — reserved baseline for 70% expected steady-state and burst autoscaling to handle peak windows; that yields better unit economics without overcommitting. we'll include an example config.
[09:55] Samir: what's the turnaround time to get results on a second benchmark? we need to plan for it.
[10:01] Jared: i can run the matrix in about 3 business days once i have the prompt set and sample load profile, deliver a write-up by 2026-01-20.
[10:10] Priya: great. also, small thing — do you have guidance on client-side multiplexing? can we multiplex across micro-batches?
[10:19] Jared: yes, and that's actually what gives a lot of the batch efficiency without increasing server-side single-request latency. client-side concurrency with batch 16 gave good results. we'll add a short note on recommended concurrency settings.
[10:35] Lidia: any mention of cost amortization for KV cache warmup? we worry the first few minutes of traffic will be expensive.
[10:44] Jared: warmup does incur higher cost; however, if you schedule a short pre-warm during predicted windows (e.g., cron-driven common prompts) you can amortize, and the runtime supports pre-warm hooks. we saw warmup penalty drop after 10-20 minutes of steady load.
[11:04] Priya: could you quantify that? like a percent penalty for the first hour?
[11:10] Jared: roughly 10-15% higher tokens/sec$ in the first 30 minutes in our test, then it stabilizes. exact depends on your cache hit rate.
[11:21] Maya: let's talk risks — what would you say is the biggest gating issue for you?
[11:27] Priya: main thing is predictability of unit costs for budget sign-off and the compliance side (KMS and audit). second is model quality under q4 quantization.
[11:36] Kenzo: and from platform view, we need clarity on VPC/private networking and whether the control plane calls home.
[11:43] Maya: all noted — i'll include both networking and KMS sections in the doc.
[11:50] Jared: one thing we can do in the next benchmark is include both hosted and dedicated runs with identical load patterns so you can see the delta directly.
[11:59] Priya: that would be ideal. also, can you include a sensitivity table for batch sizes vs p95 and tokens/sec$?
[12:07] Jared: yep — batch 1/8/16/64 across q8/q4 and caching on/off, same sample traffic. that'll be the matrix.
[12:17] Lidia: timeline recap?
[12:20] Maya: SE runs benchmark after we get prompt set, deliver by 2026-01-20. AE sends pricing and security docs by 2026-01-15. Customer to share prompts and traffic by 2026-01-18. we'll meet next Tuesday to review results, same time.
[12:38] Priya: sounds good.

Action items (as read back):
[12:45] Maya: repeating — Jared runs the benchmark matrix; Priya shares prompts/traffic; Maya sends pricing and security notes; Kenzo confirms VPC/Private preference.

[13:02] Samir: one quick Q before we wrap — if we keep hosted but enable customer-managed KMS, is that supported?
[13:08] Jared: hosted with CMK is supported in our private deployment variant; for fully hosted we can do envelope encryption and a KMS integration with limited control, we'll clarify in the doc.
[13:20] Priya: okay thanks.
[13:22] Maya: great — we're at 42 minutes; appreciate everyone's time. i'll drop the doc and the sheet after the call. thanks all.

Recap and next steps in chat: Maya will post pricing & security links; Jared will post benchmark plan & subsequent results; Priya will upload prompt set.

Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., 'K V cash' for KV cache) and filler words preserved.

End of transcript.
